Title: How does Extremis Boon actually work?

Messages.Author: Killiam
Messages.Body:
Just realized that Extremis Boon does not actually explain how it keeps you in the game, as it does not explain what pool you receive. I assume that you somehow get pool as a result of the bidding, but if that's the case, do you get all the pool from all the bidders, or only the pool offered by the highest bidder?

Thanks,
-Bill

Name: Extremis Boon
[BH:R]
Cardtype: Master
Master: out-of-turn. Boon.
Only usable when you are being ousted. Other Methuselahs may bid pool to keep you in the game. If one does, put this card in play. As a master phase action, the high bidder may steal up to 2 pool from you. You may burn this card by giving that Methuselah 6 pool during your master phase.
Artist: David Day

Messages.Author: Kilrauko
Messages.Body:
For what it's worth, the few times it's came up in "fun" decks we've handled the bidding similar to one in.

> Name: Hostile Takeover
> [Jyhad:R, VTES:R, CE:R, KoT:R]
> Cardtype: Master
> Clan: Ventrue
> Cost: 1 pool
> Master.
> Choose a vampire with capacity of 6 or less. Each Methuselah bids pool for control of that vampire. The highest bid goes to the vampire's controller; that bidder then takes control of the vampire. If the controller wins, half the winning bid (rounded up) goes to the blood bank.
> Artist: Mike Raabe; James Stowe
>
As it was natural to use Jyhad era bidding method. This reply also serves as my reminder to check when official ruling comes in as it affects a card I played and play perhaps once a year (or blue moon).

Messages.Author: ICL
Messages.Body:
So, an incoming pool loss is happening and this card interrupts that by giving everyone a chance to boost your pool before the loss occurs? In other words, blood counter related ousting effect is queued up rather than ousting having actually occurred?

True, not likely to matter, as every time I play Extremis Boon it just gets Suddened by my prey, anyway.

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> ICL wrote:
> So, an incoming pool loss is happening and this card interrupts that by giving everyone a chance to boost your pool before the loss occurs? In other words, blood counter related ousting effect is queued up rather than ousting having actually occurred.
>
LSJ's "when X is happening" wording tends to map to Ankha's "if X would happen, Y happens instead". See www.vekn.net/forum/rules-questions/76594-lost-kindred-faq

So you end up in a situation of "If you would be ousted, do a bid-pool-to-save-you-but-get-ousted-if-that-doesn't-happen instead".

It can't be a "is about to be..." in Ankha's templating, because the thing that's about to happen still happens - you just wedge something else in before it.
